name: BrauKunstHaus Zillertal Bier Zell
kurzbeschreibung: BrauKunstHaus in Zell am Ziller: Tyrol's most modern beer experience centre spanning over 5,000 m² with brewing arts, Tyrolean cultural heritage, and tastings.
beschreibung:
Overview

The forward-thinking BrauKunstHaus is located in the traditional market town of Zell am Ziller in the heart of the Tyrolean Zillertal (Schwaz district) at an altitude of approximately 575 metres. Built on the premises of the historic private brewery Zillertal Bier—Tyrol's oldest private brewery, whose brewing heritage dates back to the year 1500—this visitor centre opened in 2020 and offers an interactive multimedia experience area spanning over 5,000 square metres. Serving as a captivating synthesis of living brewing craft, regional farming, authentic Zillertal folk culture, and cutting-edge food technology, it is one of the most innovative excursion destinations in the Alps.

Interactive Tour & Beer Culture

On a self-guided tour featuring interactive multimedia exhibits, visitors immerse themselves in the craftsmanship of master brewers. Starting with the premium raw ingredients—pure Zillertal spring water from high-alpine springs, finest Tyrolean brewing grains grown under contract with regional farmers, and selected hops—the route leads directly into the ultra-modern brewhouse. Through floor-to-ceiling panoramic glass panels, guests observe brewmasters hard at work around gleaming copper brew coppers. Special attention is dedicated to sustainability: the brewery operates with a climate-conscious focus utilizing closed-loop energy systems. Alongside the brewing craft, the exhibition highlights the multi-faceted identity of the Zillertal: original archival films and audio recordings illuminate the iconic Zeller Gauder Fest—Austria's oldest spring and traditional costume festival—as well as the celebrated local musical heritage and rural life. The crowning finale of the circuit is the inviting Bräustüberl tasting area: here, visitors and certified beer sommeliers tap freshly brewed, award-winning beer specialities (such as Zillertal Gauder Steinbock, Märzen, or naturally cloudy Zwickl) paired with regional Zillertal hay-milk cheese and crisp pretzels.

Visit & Getting There

BrauKunstHaus in Zell am Ziller is open year-round from Monday to Saturday from 10:00 to 18:00 (closed on Sundays and public holidays; last admission for the tour at 16:30). Admission prices including tasting (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €12.50, youths (aged 16 to 17) approx. €10.00, children (aged 6 to 15, includes lemonade) approx. €6.00, small children free; family ticket approx. €28.00. Holders of the regional Zillertal Activcard receive a discount. The adjacent brewery shop is freely accessible. Arriving by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Zillertal), continue along the B169 valley road for roughly 20 km to Zell am Ziller and follow signs to the brewery (large free car park at Talstraße 26). By public transport: take the Zillertalbahn railway to Bahnhof Zell am Ziller, from where it is just a three-minute stroll directly to the entrance.

Tips

The entire BrauKunstHaus is designed to be barrier-free, offering step-free access for wheelchairs and strollers via modern elevators. For children, an entertaining riddle passport invites young detectives on a playful discovery tour through the exhibits. Take advantage of the attached brewery boutique to purchase exclusive speciality beers, elegant glassware, and regional Zillertal gourmet treats as souvenirs.
